proposedMechanism: Keep canonical class/definitions/dependency closure/eager imports untouched. Add contentRendering: 'eager' | 'on-demand' (content-rendering), default eager; author before the first update. This is a construction policy, not a definition profile/code boundary.

Always call dialogTemplate with the existing dialogView. Change only its generated body argument. Before activation pass an empty TemplateResult, not undefined (undefined restores authored default slot). No generic authored-content deferral.

Use a per-instance retained body-activated bit. Candidate media-local implementation wraps protected requestOpen in a synchronous depth counter and try/finally around super.requestOpen; willUpdate may latch only at depth zero with open true. This avoids a shared superclass API solely for one candidate. Alternative is a shared settled-open hook owned by Stage B. Define release as first rendering that observes settled accepted open: synchronous show(); hide() or open=true; open=false before render leaves unused body absent. This is intentionally narrower than any accepted transition permanently releasing construction.

Never gate or latch solely on this.open: it is deliberately tentative during en-change, and listeners may call performUpdate. Canceled/superseded open must leave a previously unused body absent. Do not duplicate dispatchChange or convert show/hide to Promise.

Initial open=true from author/SSR snapshot must render the body on the matching first render. Silent authoritative writes, nested transactions, same-value writes and removal/reconnect require explicit regressions before accepting the local-depth proposal.

Keep retained body after close so zoom/pan/current slide/native nodes and carousel ownership retain existing behavior. activeKey and items still update/reset according to existing methods before or after activation.

No optional-code preparation operation is needed here: existing tag load/ensure remain separate. A common code-only prepare must not activate body, open or focus any instance. Do not advertise a fake optional-code saving or mount siblings when one opens.

Readiness is separate from synchronous show outcome. For measurements, observe accepted native modality/focus plus selected decoded image and operative carousel/tools; do not delay and replay the initial native interaction or add late focus choreography.

A body constructed under eager policy must also count as activated; a later policy write cannot remove existing body. Freeze how unsupported late policy writes are handled through common API contract. Per-request SSR component instances start fresh; do not reuse previously opened server instances without carrying matching construction state.
requiredFunctionalCells: Default eager produces same body before open; explicit on-open omits only generated body; no change to pure/eager import or registration graphs.

Canceled first show with synchronous performUpdate/update flush leaves body absent; canceled hide retains body/open; nested/superseding open/close and authoritative same-value writes obey dispatchChange.
show(); hide() and open=true; open=false in one turn before rendering leave the unused body absent; after actual body construction, closing or subsequent policy writes never remove it.
Programmatic show/hide retain synchronous ChangeOutcome; open property and initial open attribute are silent; preview click activeKey then show selects requested image; no contentless visible modal.

First opening before optional descendants finish their update has correct shell focus and correct final usable controls; no late focus theft; Escape/close-button/backdrop policy and for= focus return stay unchanged.

Media en-change cancellation and author writes preserve accepted key and view resets; item removal/replacement before first open and while open uses current model; empty items retain No media available behavior.
Zoom/pan/pointercancel and repeated close/open retain state/node identity exactly as eager reference; disconnected gestures cannot act later.

Remove before pending render/readiness, reconnect, adopt same-origin document, two viewers sharing a registry, nested ordinary/shadow scopes, null dormancy and actual unsupported-engine global fallback. Opening one viewer must not construct sibling bodies.

SSR initial eager closed, opt-in closed and opt-in open, same initial snapshot hydration identity, streamed containing owner, pre-hydration trigger policy; fresh items assigned after hydration. Existing description SSR fixture has no media items and cannot prove media body hydration.

contractSketch.publicPolicy: Stage A alignment: additive contentRendering: eager | on-demand, attribute content-rendering. Default eager; construction only with static dependencies/imports unchanged. Require policy before first update, and require SSR/first client snapshot agreement. Do not silently repurpose loading/items.

contractSketch.entryProfiles: Canonical tag class/definition imports, dependency closure and registration remain identical. Metadata can advertise construction policy and no optional code loader. Selective imports remain usable without full manifest.
contractSketch.loadPrepare: Existing tag load/preparation may load code only and cannot construct rows, focus, upgrade a dormant instance, open, change accepted values or announce opening. Since optional code is not split, optional-code cold/prepared performance cells are explicitly not applicable, not zero-cost success claims.
contractSketch.instanceMechanism: One per-instance monotonic rowsUsed boolean, derived showRows = contentRendering === eager || rowsUsed. Set rowsUsed synchronously when the first valid semantic open request is accepted, before its scheduled render; no Promise or separate loader/cache/state machine. Preserve stable native input, popup/listbox shell and same-root labels. Retain rows after first accepted opening and construction, including when closed; subsequent catalog changes reconcile keyed rows exactly as eager behavior.
notChanged: No deferred native editor/control or form adapter.
No per-instance registry and no new generated custom-element dependency.
No implicit intersection scanner, prefetch scheduler or URL loading.
No data fetcher, remote result window or virtualization.
No new await/replay of a trusted native action.
No change to synchronous focus/select/validity/reset or transactional events.

Arrow key handler opens and moves the active model synchronously; rendered active-descendant must reference an existing row only when popup is presented. First ArrowDown and immediate ArrowUp while layout is pending already have regression tests.
Opening must preserve focused native query. Typing only filters; it never accepts a catalog ID. Empty/disabled/unavailable item rules and last known label remain current.
On canceled en-change, keep native query/selection/popup; author value writes supersede rollback and close/reconcile. Catalog replacement during a transaction cannot accept obsolete candidates.

Keep popup shell identity so Popover/fallback setup, beforetoggle, exit paint and first-use layout measurement have existing ownership. PositionController and outside-dismissal resources already start only while open.
While loading/error blocks suggestions, construction state must not create fake selectable rows. Loading/error is application catalog state, not delivery state.
Reset/restore/disable/readonly/disconnect close intent. A queued Lit update after removal must not open/focus; no async import exists but lifecycle races still need regression coverage.
multiselect: Opening can happen on query click, input, Enter when closed, Arrow navigation, and authoritative changes may reset active choice. Gate only picker kind; checkbox-group/toggle-group/selection-collection retain normal visible alternatives.
Preserve #query identity and its current live(query) behavior, including hydrationQuery capture in first willUpdate; do not add competing EditingController as part of the lazy-row change.
Selected tags and their remove buttons stay eager and independently operable while options are absent. Repeated form values, required/unavailable validation and default/reset stay synchronous.

Keep #choices shell and ensure expanded aria-activedescendant resolves to an existing row after first render. New option rows use the original keyed repeat and same labels/IDs; no remote/windowed results.
Authored en-choice-option metadata remains in the authored tree and the SelectionChildrenController keeps its current synchronous catalog/SSR snapshot duties, even before option buttons exist.
Current outside-pointer listener attaches on connection even while closed; separating that listener is a distinct runtime-resource opportunity and must not be conflated with option DOM savings.

proposedMechanism.apiSketchOnly: Use agreed contentRendering: eager|on-demand, attribute content-rendering, eager default; configure pre-first-update. Earlier spelling suggestions are superseded.
proposedMechanism.renderBoundary: Keep the dialogTemplate and command body wrapper/default slot stable. Gate the generated label, focus-frame/input, listbox/options and polite status inside commandPaletteTemplate. Preserve named/default authored slots, IDs of mounted generated descendants and keyed rows.
proposedMechanism.activation: Mark an instance constructed only after accepted opening or an authoritative open=true write, before the next opening render. Do not infer acceptance merely from tentative this.open inside render; en-change listeners can synchronously flush Lit while open is tentative. Use acceptance-owned hooks/overrides around requestOpen and the authoritative open setter, preserving revision semantics. Inherited show()/hide() remain synchronous ChangeOutcome APIs with no Promise or deferred native gesture replay.
proposedMechanism.initialOpen: Initial server/client open=true is immediately eligible for generated content; native modality still begins through existing connected/updated syncDialog lifecycle.
proposedMechanism.stickyRetention: Once built, retain the native editor and generated root through close/reopen/removal/reconnect. Do not detach/recreate to reclaim nodes: accepted-close reset, orphaned composition and node identity are existing contracts. Switching policy after materialization cannot destroy content.
proposedMechanism.preparation: Shared code preparation remains load-only and does not set construction eligibility. No new import cache/controller/scheduler is needed. Existing app readiness then authoritative open works unchanged.
proposedMechanism.catalog: Keep atomic commandSnapshot and model ownership before first use. Deferring model creation/filtering is a separate CPU/data proposal that is not justified by this construction design.
proposedMechanism.failure: No network or new async construction failure state added. Existing tag-level load/ensure failure UI remains application-owned. Incompatible SSR/client construction configuration must be diagnosed by shared profile agreement before destructive reconciliation.
proposedMechanism.scopes: Same constructor/definition and owning registry as eager. No per-instance registry, global retry, registration side effect from profile preparation, or sibling construction.

contracts.obligation: Preserve tentative en-change, rollback, equal authoritative writes, nested accepted transitions, ChangeOutcome return, deferred native modality and opener restoration.
Accepted close restores focus before combobox ARIA/reset; hydration reads retained input rather than overwriting it.
Full synchronous en-action dispatch precedes default close; cancel action/close or equal author write preserves ownership. Current enabled catalog is rechecked.
No Lit .value writer; native text, selection, composition and interaction reset remain owned by current editor/controller.
Validation/copying stays atomic before/after mount. Query/candidate replacement and disabled action rules unchanged.
Same finite snapshot/profile server/client; pure imports/initial rendering; no document work, fetch, scheduling or modality during SSR.
button/icon dependencies remain declared once. Keeping shell eager means no claim to defer those dependencies.
No additional savings claimed from existing open-only listeners and geometry.

proposedAcceptanceGates.state: Proposals only, not frozen or measured. Integration owner must freeze exact workloads, builds, reference/candidate hashes, thresholds and contention protocol before candidate timing.
proposedAcceptanceGates.samplePlan: At least 30 successful samples per timing cell/configuration; retain every failure/abort. Report n, median, p75, spread/uncertainty. p95 only with at least 100 samples. Retention separately: five fresh-context repetitions per arm, 100 open/close cycles, compare cycles 10 and 100.
proposedAcceptanceGates.deterministicConstruction: Opted-in never-open instances have 0 generated comboboxes, 0 generated listboxes, 0 command options and 0 generated search-status nodes. After first accepted open exactly 1 combobox, 1 listbox and the exact eligible rows; opening one of 10 opted-in siblings constructs only that instance. Eager default DOM remains unchanged. Canceled first open constructs 0 generated search nodes unless an authoritative or nested accepted transition explicitly supersedes it.
proposedAcceptanceGates.componentBenefit: Unused connected DOM reduction >=20 nodes and >=20% of complete palette inclusive shadow descendant nodes on the real four-command settings catalog. Count light/shadow nodes consistently; retain live/inert/detached counts separately.
proposedAcceptanceGates.routeBenefit: For route adoption require unused whole-route connected DOM reduction >=2%, and initial-ready median improvement >=max(2 ms, 3% of matched eager). A component pass without the whole-route pass is not route promotion.
proposedAcceptanceGates.firstUse: Same-code construction-only palette action-to-ready p75 <=100 ms, p75 regression <=max(8 ms, 10% of eager); at 4x declared CPU throttling p75 <=200 ms and regression <=max(16 ms, 10%). Readiness includes actual modality, search focus, visible current catalog and correct ARIA. Additive profile overhead on eager median <=max(1 ms, 2%).
proposedAcceptanceGates.repeat: Repeat action-to-ready p75 regression <=max(2 ms, 5% of eager); native input object identity unchanged across all 100 close/reopen cycles and reconnect checks.
proposedAcceptanceGates.bytes: Construction-only candidate adds 0 requests; route transferred/evaluated bytes remain identical aside from documented profile/policy implementation overhead bounded at <=1024 gzip bytes. No optional-code saving claim without separately proving a unique emitted chunk on the real route.
proposedAcceptanceGates.retention: For each repetition, cycle-10 to cycle-100 live node/listener count growth is 0 and candidate detached-node growth <= matched eager + 2 nodes. Post-GC heap delta growth <=max(64 KiB, 1% of cycle-10 candidate heap) and no retained removed hosts attributable to shared state. Report raw counts and noise; gate failure is not repaired by selected replacement runs.
proposedAcceptanceGates.trafficPreparation: Compare eager tag path, construction-only identical code, existing cold tag code+registration, and explicitly prepared tag code. Report 0/50/200 ms preparation leads plus never-used preparation; preparation is not opening, and hidden early traffic is not a startup benefit. Tag-code cold/prepared cases use separately frozen shared loader budgets.

qualificationMatrix: All existing command/dialog/SSR tests in affected closure plus opt-in counterparts; serialized supported entry points with fresh EN_EXECUTION_OUTPUT and ownership leases.

Real settings route current action execution and loading/retry/Escape/focus-generation guard behavior. No shared-bundle saving inferred from isolated module fixture.
One-at-a-time manual first-open focus/announcement fixture for changed behavior; DOM focus and synthetic composition do not establish screen-reader or physical-IME acceptance.
command-palette-design.nextOwnerAction: Shared API/integration owner chooses stable construction policy naming and freezes gates; implementation owner builds focused sticky construction candidate; validation owner qualifies real settings/showcase workloads. Leave the row unfinished until promoted or evidence-backed rejected.

compact-overlay-design.head: fba5ec19b58606cf1776df44862a38a3898f4c72
compact-overlay-design.method: Read-only source audit. No tests, browser, timing, generated metadata changes, or product edits. All numeric gates below are proposed before experiments; none are measured results. JSON is an agent handoff, not the completed rollout disposition.

common_contract.default: Existing eager rendering and import/definition graph remain unchanged unless the consumer explicitly opts into a versioned generated-content construction feature.
common_contract.boundary: Separate construction state from tag code load, registration, ready state and semantic opening. These candidates expose no unique optional code split from the inspected implementation; do not claim transfer savings or invent async semantic APIs.
common_contract.data: Consumer arrays and scalar page state are already resident. Deferring generated DOM does not defer array retrieval, data allocation, filtering, server serialization of data, or registration. No application data loader belongs in these components.
common_contract.registration: Keep existing definitions/dependencies and same constructors; existing scoped registry owner is inherited. Do not create per-instance registries or call registerAll inside features.
common_contract.hydration: Opt-in initial render state must match server and client snapshot exactly. Instance-local activated state cannot be reconstructed from module globals. Preserve authored nodes and native first-paint semantics; server construction savings and browser construction savings must be reported separately.
common_contract.retention: Retain first-use generated nodes after close for identity/focus/draft safety; prune only data identities actually removed under existing author update semantics. Disconnect/adoption must cancel pending presentation work. Late async state must not mount or focus detached/rebound instances.
common_contract.synchronous: Never change existing synchronous show/hide/change returns to promises. Prepare generated content within the same synchronous opening lifecycle, or guard presentation internally after the semantic transaction while preserving its immediate return. Never await then replay native activation.
common_contract.numeric_protocol: For any promoted claim: freeze exact source/lock/runtime/browser/harness and budgets first; at least 30 successful timings per configuration, retain failures/aborts, report median/p75/spread; do not publish p95 below n=100. Five fresh contexts per retention arm, 100 cycles each, compare cycle 10 to 100. Construction-only candidates compare identical loaded code; cold/prepared code arms are not applicable unless a real separate dependency is found.

candidates.feature: Generated menu items for unopened root command menus
candidates.qualification_status: source-assessed; worth qualifying; no final rollout disposition yet
candidates.eager_cost: The menubar repeats every root button, every en-menu shell and every en-menu-item in every item.items array on its first render, although all root menus start closed. Cost scales with the sum of all command counts. Generated en-menu-item construction/upgrade/inner DOM are the removable work; retaining root en-menu shells retains their controllers and trigger discovery.
candidates.code_vs_data: menubar imports EnMenu only as a type, but menubarDefinition statically declares menuDefinition and menuItemDefinition. There is no existing lazy loader or unique optional implementation branch. All command arrays remain application data and remain available. Construction-only deferral does not remove menu/menu-item modules from the entry graph.
candidates.mechanism: Add opt-in generated-items construction policy with an instance-local activated-root key set; retain every root button and en-menu shell so same-tree for references and trigger listeners work immediately. Render item.items only for activated keys. On any first open proposal, prepare the generated commands before menu child discovery, positioning and focus; then retain them across close/reopen. Key activation by stable item.value rather than trigger index and reconcile removed keys. An implementation must cover both menubar switchTo and EnMenu-owned trigger click/ArrowDown/ArrowUp; a switchTo-only implementation misses direct trigger listeners.
candidates.design_obligation: A private owner readiness handshake between generated-content owner and EnMenu is safer than an async show wrapper. EnMenu show() synchronously returns dispatchChange outcome; native presentation happens later through updated/syncPopover. If a synchronous en-change handler schedules the parent construction render, prove ordering through child update/readChildren/positioning rather than assuming MutationObserver/slotchange fires before focus. Cancellation or authoritative open writes must still resolve immediately. The native presentation must never show an empty menu or steal focus after the user moves away. This audit does not assert such a handshake already exists.
triggers: Native root button click/Enter/Space handled by each EnMenu trigger connection
ArrowDown/ArrowUp handled by EnMenu and menubar key path
ArrowLeft/ArrowRight with an open menu and pointer hover across roots via switchTo
Internal generated EnMenu show() and silent open writes if supported by a documented internal owner path
candidates.fallback: Default stays eager. Opt-in keeps real labelled menubar buttons and trigger semantics present at initial render. This application command widget already requires JavaScript for execution; commands absent in a lazy SSR branch must not be advertised as browser Find/print-equivalent authored content. All content here is data-generated, not user-authored slots.
candidates.ssr_ownership: SSR must render the same unopened generated-items branch as initial client hydration. Menubar owns generated light DOM of each generated EnMenu; EnMenu owns its native popover/slot and focus behavior. No island or second hydration owner may be inserted around individual command children.
candidates.boundedness: Unbounded consumer command count; unopened command bodies are the only large source-backed opportunity here. Root shells remain O(root count). Activated key set must be pruned when roots are removed to avoid monotonic key accumulation.

actual_consumers.size: Two root menus with two commands each; uses catalog registerAll at route entry. No external real application adoption or occasional-use frequency is established by this source.

required_qualification: Actual docs root menu click, ArrowDown, ArrowUp last-item entry, left/right RTL traversal, hover switch, Escape/outside/Tab dismissal and original action identity
Cancelable close when changing roots; canceled/superseded first open; disabled/replaced data before construction; rapid cross-root intent and focus movement
Remove/reconnect/adopt menubar before internal readiness; independent/scoped registry ownership and mixed eager/lazy sibling menus
SSR marker/node identity for shells with matching opt-in snapshot; eager SSR parity remains unchanged
Compare actual four-command consumer first; larger fixture may establish scaling but cannot replace real route benefit

proposed_numeric_gates.component_never_used: At least 20% fewer recursively connected component nodes and at least 24 fewer nodes at idle versus identical eager code. Count generated item constructors separately; zero constructors for unopened command items. If actual four-command route cannot reach this, do not invent a larger adoption workload.
proposed_numeric_gates.whole_route: At least 5% fewer recursively connected route nodes and at least 32 absolute nodes saved on the actual consuming route; startup median and p75 no more than 5% worse. Component qualification alone does not permit route adoption.
proposed_numeric_gates.first_use: Action-to-ready p75 <=50 ms and incremental p75 over eager <=32 ms; median incremental <=16 ms. Ready includes expected first/last item focus and final usable menu geometry.
proposed_numeric_gates.repeat: Repeat action-to-ready p75 <=eager p75+8 ms; no additional generated item construction for unchanged already-used keys.
proposed_numeric_gates.retention: After cycles 10 to 100, zero additional generated elements/listeners for a fixed data set; same retained item identities; median post-GC heap growth <=64 KiB per arm, subject to predeclared measurement noise protocol.

candidates.qualification_status: source-assessed; design-sensitive candidate requiring actual opportunity qualification; no final rollout disposition yet
candidates.eager_cost: The measurement rack always constructs one native button per item plus a More button. count begins Infinity, so the first live row also constructs every action before measurement. Once measured, actions after count render as another repeat inside closed details .extra. Merely making the later .extra conditional cannot claim startup construction savings: every action was already built in the first live row.
candidates.code_vs_data: One compact static class using native details/buttons and visibleActionCount; no generated child custom elements or unique optional code subtree. Item array and measurement data remain resident. Measurement buttons are essential for exact arbitrary labels/themes/font sizes; changing them is a separate layout algorithm, not lazy delivery.
candidates.mechanism: Construction candidate must be explicit about the unknown-width first render. Variant A only omits never-opened .extra after width measurement; this reduces settled hidden DOM but not initial constructors and may still reduce later recreations after layout changes. Variant B begins opt-in in a deterministic unmeasured state with measurement rack and functioning More disclosure holding commands constructed on opening, then constructs only the measured visible subset; it requires new SSR/no-JS/failure and first-paint geometry qualification before any promotion. Do not silently apply Variant B to defaults or call Variant A an initial construction optimization. Keep the native details and summary mounted; materialize the extra body synchronously on summary click/keyboard activation before native default toggle, with open/toggle reconciliation for programmatic details.open changes. Retain extra nodes after first use where they remain part of the current partition.
candidates.design_obligation: Resize focus migration is an opening trigger too. Existing measure() captures a focused data-action, updates count, then finds its new row button, opens details if it moved and focuses it. A lazy partition must activate its body before that update and before the post-update query. Native summary activation and programmatic details.open must never expose an empty first-open panel. Native toggle has no synchronous cancelable semantic contract; no async replay of clicks or synthetic keypresses is acceptable. Repartitioning across independently keyed repeats currently recreates controls; new retention claims must not presume identity across partitions.
triggers: Resize/measurement moving focused action into extra
Programmatic details.open/toggle observation where existing DOM behavior is preserved
Items/labels/theme/font/container changes requiring measurement and redistribution
candidates.fallback: Eager default remains a complete SSR action row. Variant A keeps that. Variant B cannot be promoted until an explicit no-JS/failure reading/action fallback exists and matches SSR/client; otherwise keep the conservative initial eager row and report narrower settled-DOM opportunity honestly.
candidates.ssr_ownership: Current server has count Infinity and does not know browser width; it renders all live actions plus inert measurement rack, with no details. Hydration must match that unless a separately documented opt-in branch intentionally changes initial state. Native controls are library-generated; consumer has no authored slot subtree here.
candidates.boundedness: At steady state the only omitted controls are N-visibleCount, but the mandatory rack stays O(N). Existing actual example is five actions and may have no extras at a wide viewport. First-use/width must be declared with any claimed savings. No saving is possible on a route whose actions all fit.

actual_consumers.size: Five actions; disclosure only appears when measured width requires it; catalog registered eagerly on this route.

required_qualification: Declare wide and narrow actual consumer widths; count first-render constructions separately from settled DOM and later layout churn
Summary native mouse/keyboard and rapid close/open; first Tab reaches first enabled extra; Escape returns focus to summary
Focused visible action migrating into extra during shrink, extra returning to row on grow, removed/disabled focused actions, changed action data and cancellation-free exact action identity
Zero use, repeated use and reconnection with ResizeObserver cleanup; font/theme sizing changes preserve visibleActionCount decisions
SSR/no-JS markup and hydration initial branch; independent generated DOM ownership; no modifications to authored nodes

proposed_numeric_gates.component_never_used: For Variant B startup claims: >=20% fewer recursively connected component nodes and >=10 absolute nodes/constructed controls saved for actual consumer at a declared narrow width, counting the mandatory measurement rack in both arms. Variant A may qualify only settled-DOM reduction, never initial construction savings; require >=20% and >=10 nodes saved after measurement.
proposed_numeric_gates.whole_route: At least 5% fewer recursively connected route nodes and at least 32 absolute nodes on actual route; initial visible action geometry must differ by <=1 CSS px once ready; startup median/p75 <=eager*1.05.
proposed_numeric_gates.first_use: Summary action-to-ready p75 <=50 ms and <=eager p75+16 ms; native disclosure must be populated before its first visible presentation. Resize focus migration succeeds in every functional repetition.
proposed_numeric_gates.repeat: Repeat open p75 <=eager p75+8 ms with no new controls for unchanged previously-used partition.
proposed_numeric_gates.retention: Zero cycle-10-to-100 extra generated elements/listeners for fixed items and width sequence; median post-GC heap growth <=64 KiB per arm.

candidates.qualification_status: source-assessed; bounded candidate requiring deterministic benefit screen; no final rejected disposition
candidates.eager_cost: Known totals render the native page-jump popover and its five-element descendant body (jump div, label, input, Cancel button, Go button) while closed. Unknown totals already omit all direct-entry controls. Numbered page computation is bounded to seven logical positions; huge pageCount does not create an enormous page collection.
candidates.code_vs_data: No custom child registration dependencies and no unique optional module. Native chooser and handlers live in pagination template/element; page-count is scalar state, not record loading. The current .value input binding, native validity, transactional page changes, and owner callbacks all stay together.
candidates.mechanism: If worth measured complexity, add opt-in construction flag retaining the #page-jump native popover shell and every popovertarget invoker. Gate only the five-element body until first invocation. Prepare body synchronously in the existing click/pointerdown path (click covers keyboard), and cover beforetoggle for direct native showPopover calls so native default action never opens an empty shell. Preserve native opening rather than await then replay. Retain body after close; pageCount=0 keeps its established full removal behavior and focus recovery. Do not gate numbered pages or essential Previous/Next/status.
candidates.design_obligation: A requestUpdate in click is asynchronous; qualification must prove content is ready before native popover opening and observeJump focus/position. A beforetoggle synchronous construction hook can preserve native default invocation but must not call performUpdate reentrantly during another Lit update; prepare/flush design must account for this. Native popovertarget shell needs stable identity and same-root target resolution; removing it until click can break direct invocation and declarative semantics.
triggers: Native gap/compact chooser click, Enter and Space via popovertarget
Pointerdown invoker retention followed by click
Direct native popover opening, if preserving accessible internal native behavior
Known-to-unknown count transition and disabled update while open
candidates.fallback: All essential page actions, status, boundaries, slot content and page semantics remain eagerly SSR-rendered. Default chooser remains complete. Lazy chooser body has no authored content; no records are removed from reading/Find/print. Opt-in should document JavaScript dependence consistent with pagination README, and avoid exposing a blank usable popover before hydration.
candidates.ssr_ownership: Pagination owns native shadow content; Previous/Next authored slot nodes stay owned by consumer. Server/client opt-in must agree on omitted body. If user typed before hydration in eager/default SSR, preserve existing identity; a construction opt-in must not accidentally remove an existing server input/draft.
candidates.boundedness: Exactly five descendant elements per known-total pager can be gated while retaining shell; no custom-element constructor savings. More than one hundred million pages still use at most seven logical page positions. Existing dedicated docs example has several pagers so aggregated fixed-node savings are possible, but a single workflow pager offers only five elements; neither route benefit nor no-change rejection is established by this source audit alone.

actual_consumers.size: Primary pager plus intermediate, mobile, alignment, slotted/text and unknown-total examples.

actual_consumers.note: Pager constructed even hidden when nonpaginated or <2 pages; data-table owner adoption must be explicit and may have a broader separate generated-pager construction opportunity.

required_qualification: Native popovertarget opens on first click/Enter/Space with field focus and usable positioned panel; Escape/Cancel/outside dismissal and original invoker focus
Native validity, Enter/Go, cancelable page transaction and authoritative property writes keep current behavior; canceled changes keep chooser open
Resize across wide/intermediate/compact, RTL, mobile visual viewport and nested shadow scrolling with input node identity preserved
Disabled/unknown totals while focused recover focus; reconnect/adopt before any pending readiness cannot steal focus
SSR/default no-JS labels/current page/status and hydrated native identity remain; authored previous/next slots remain present

Screen deterministic five-node-per-pager opportunity against declared actual route node totals before investing in promotion timing; if insufficient, record evidence-backed no-change rather than inventing a giant page list

proposed_numeric_gates.component_never_used: For fixed chooser body require >=10% fewer recursively connected component nodes on actual known-total pager; the absolute source ceiling is five elements, to be verified by browser DOM accounting, and zero code bytes. No unbounded page-count saving claim is allowed.
proposed_numeric_gates.whole_route: At least 5% fewer recursively connected nodes and >=32 absolute nodes saved on an actual route; dedicated multi-pager docs is a separate route from single-pager workflows. Startup median/p75 must be <=eager*1.05.
proposed_numeric_gates.first_use: Native chooser action-to-ready p75 <=50 ms and <=eager p75+8 ms, with input ready/focused by first visible chooser presentation. Five-node saving does not justify a larger first-use regression.
proposed_numeric_gates.repeat: Repeat open p75 <=eager p75+4 ms and retained input identity/draft semantics match eager.
proposed_numeric_gates.retention: Zero additional chooser elements/listeners from cycle 10 to 100 for fixed known pageCount; median post-GC heap growth <=32 KiB per arm.

compact-overlay-design.follow_up_owner_guidance: Integrating inventory owner must assign final implemented/already-conditional/essential-eager/not-applicable/rejected-with-evidence only after relevant deterministic or measured qualification. These source proposals are not permission to mark full rollout complete. Shared generated-content preparation/metadata naming belongs to common API owner; family implementations must not each introduce loaders/caches.

sharedPolicy.lifetime: retain constructed body after first accepted opening; do not tear down on close
sharedPolicy.status: Shared Stage A interface decision relayed by root; no implementation claim

toast-history-design.audit: read-only source design audit; no edits, tests, browser runs or timing measurements
toast-history-design.head: fba5ec19b58606cf1776df44862a38a3898f4c72
toast-history-design.classification: construction-only candidate; public history feature is already conditional; no verified consumer-benefit or promotion disposition in this audit

sourceFacts.finding: history boolean is public; recent and waiting state are per instance; historyItems synchronously returns copied records; clearHistory synchronously replaces recent with [] and schedules render; retention clamps to 0..1000 or 20 for invalid values.
Default history=false, historyLimit=20. Existing eager defaults must remain unchanged.

sync retains accepted closed snapshots only while history=true, tracks prior open state, updates active/waiting presentation, queues announcements for admitted messages, and derives plain waiting message strings independently of the history disclosure.
Recent capture requires previous recorded open state and current open===false; preserve snapshot observation timing and retention behavior while deferring only construction.

en-change processing queues a microtask; MutationObserver/updated/firstUpdated drive synchronization. Snapshot getter is synchronous over current recorded state, but captures are not promised synchronously inside the original dismissal listener. Disable-history and limit trimming occur in updated.

history=false omits details entirely. history=true creates native details without open binding; summary, all waiting <li>s, all retained recent <li>s and clear en-button are constructed even while disclosure is closed. No toggle handler exists.
notify returns created element immediately; insertion waits initial empty persistent announcers. Admission announcements and persistent status/alert nodes must remain outside history construction.
Region static dependency is toast, whose static dependencies include button and icon. Clear button already follows that graph; construction deferral must not imply module/registration savings.

Dismissal is synchronous cancelable staging; plain message text excludes slotted actions; queue admission independently controls timeout. History previews must neither replay interactive DOM nor promote waiting toasts.

Documented native keyboard disclosure, no announcement replay, previews do not affect admission/timers, copied snapshots, closure ordering, clearing, instance-only ownership and clear-button focus retention.

consumers.shape: history=true, history-limit=5, initial one authored open toast, max starts3. User controls create messages; reset clears history. Initial source workload has zero retained rows and zero queued rows. This real route does not establish a large initial-row benefit.
toastExample is the interactive Notifications and toast actions catalogue entry.
toast and toast-region API pages share a history guide, and link to isolated toast example.
Settings notification region has no history opt-in; no construction savings from this feature.
Theme proof notifications region has no history opt-in.

ssrOwnership.finding: Adapter records max per renderer/request with request-local Map and nonce, annotates authored/forwarded queued children and stack summary, and does not derive history rows. Do not add shared state, move authored nodes, change open/hidden, or introduce another hydration owner.

Fresh instance history arrays start empty. Persistent announcers render empty, authored messages stay readable and server stack annotations preserve state. New opt-in initial lazy branch must match server/client; existing SSR tests are source evidence only, not run for this audit.

proposedMechanism.interface: contentRendering: 'eager' | 'on-demand', attribute content-rendering; set before first update; default eager
proposedMechanism.scope: Only library-generated history body/list construction while history=true. Keep authored notification slot, stack summary, history details/summary, retention/copy/clear APIs, static definitions and announcement/timer machinery eager.
proposedMechanism.mount: For on-demand, observe native details toggle without preventDefault or gesture replay; first native open latches construction. Pointer, Enter/Space activation and programmatic details.open must be covered. Observe an already-open native details at first update/hydration so pre-hydration interaction is preserved. No controlled .open binding.
proposedMechanism.retention: Retain constructed body across close/reopen after first open; never destroy focused clear button during ordinary data clear. Preserve existing history=false subtree removal and snapshot clearing; latch state remains instance-local and sticky under the agreed contract.
proposedMechanism.preparation: No dynamic import, async API, new cache or registry operation is justified for this boundary. Module code and generated child dependencies remain eager. A shared content-rendering opt-in controls only construction.
proposedMechanism.synchronousContract: historyItems immediately reflects current recorded snapshots before first open; clearHistory empties stored recent records immediately, including while closed/unconstructed. Do not postpone data capture, retention clamps, pending additions, cancelable dismissal, focus recovery or queuedCount.
proposedMechanism.adoptionLifecycle: Use a local bound toggle handler through Lit template, no global listeners, shared Signals or additional timers. Reconnect/adoption must not reset recorded snapshots or sticky construction beyond existing behavior; history opt-out continues current clearing semantics.
proposedMechanism.firstOpenRisk: Native toggle fires after native state changes. Qualify no empty visible history body/frame at first reveal and no click/keyboard regression; do not claim first-open readiness from load()/ensure().

proposedNumericGates.status: PREDECLARED PROPOSALS ONLY: no measurements, accepted budgets, or performance claims from this audit
proposedNumericGates.workloads: Keep real toast route (5 recent limit, max3, initial 1 message) as actual consumer evidence. Use 20-recent +20-waiting typical stress and 1000-recent+100-waiting hard stress only as synthetic component evidence; do not substitute them for a real route benefit.
proposedNumericGates.initialConstruction: Before first open with opt-in: exactly 0 generated history li nodes; eager and post-open arms must render exactly waiting+retained snapshot count. Preserve all authored notification element identities. Require >=40% reduction of history-body element nodes and >=50 fewer total constructed elements at a qualifying real deferred-use consumer before promotion as a worthwhile consumer optimization.
proposedNumericGates.startupCost: Matched initial route readiness median must improve >=5% with uncertainty excluding a regression; p75 regression allowance <=5% and <=5ms. A route initially having zero history entries cannot satisfy the row-construction benefit gate by synthetic seeding.
proposedNumericGates.firstUse: At typical qualified workload: first-open content-ready p75 <=100ms and added cost versus eager <=50ms. At hard-cap stress: p75 <=200ms and no individual task >100ms. These are proposed gates to freeze before timing, not current observations.
proposedNumericGates.traffic: Unique module/request saving target is exactly 0; require zero additional requests or delayed registration for this construction-only boundary. Do not claim code-load benefit.
proposedNumericGates.retention: Five fresh-context arms, 100 open/close cycles each; compare cycle10 to100: no growth in generated row count for unchanged records, 0 additional retained event listeners, heap growth <=5% and <=1MiB after identical collection protocol. Sticky retained first-use body is expected, repeated-cycle growth is not.
proposedNumericGates.sampling: At least30 successful timing samples/configuration with all failures retained; report n, median, p75 and uncertainty, not p95 unless n>=100. Declare exact reference/candidate locks, source/build/runtime/browser identities before campaign.

qualificationNeeded: Real history consumer with sufficient unopened retained/backlog rows; current docs route initial source establishes no such benefit.
Eager/default parity; opt-in absent rows before first open; updates/clear before first open; history=false reset; clamps0/20/1000; historyItems copy mutation cannot mutate storage.

Native pointer, Enter, Space and programmatic open; no-JS/SSR/default content; pre-hydration opening; no redundant live-region announcements; clear retains focus; no waiting toast admission or timer changes.
Vetoed/accepted dismissals, timeout and silent author close; removal exclusion; forwarded slots; scoped owning registration; reconnect/adoption and simultaneous regions; request isolation.
Existing test extension anchors apps/docs/tests/toast.spec.ts:296-311 and packages/ssr/tests/toast.test.mjs:11-33. These tests were inspected, not executed.
Because native interaction timing changes, provide a ready fixture for short human keyboard/assistive-technology check; DOM/AX assertions cannot prove spoken output.
toast-history-design.recommendation: Implement only if shared content-rendering machinery and a qualifying deferred-use consumer justify cost. No unique code boundary; core toast delivery, timers, data retention and announcers are essential eager. The existing empty-initial docs consumer provides deterministic no-initial-row-benefit evidence, so do not claim promoted consumer benefit merely from the 1000-snapshot cap.

budgetDecision.scope: Every numeric family gate in this file is adopted as written. Historical estimates are source opportunities, not measurements.
budgetDecision.precedence: Per-family gates here govern media, selection, commands, menubar, overflow, pagination and toast. Contextual toolbar uses editor.md. Shared API/date protocol uses budgets.json. Generic constructionFeature in budgets.json is only a template and does not override a named family.
budgetDecision.changeRule: Changes require a new declared candidate/protocol before new measurements; existing failures and thresholds remain preserved.
